Abstract 29

Disease-modifying therapies for Tauopathies like Alzheimer’s disease have targeted 30

Tau hyperphosphorylation and aggregation, as both pathological manifestations are implicated 31

in Tau-mediated toxicity. More recently there has been a renewed interest in Tau conformation 32

which appears to influence its toxic potential. However, the impact of Tau hyper- 33

phosphorylation on its eventual conformation and toxic potential is less well known. 34

Leveraging the genetic tractability of Drosophila, we generated multiple inducible 35

human Tau transgenes with altered phosphorylation status and/or aggregation propensity.  Their 36

individual and combined impact was tested in vivo by quantifying Tau misfolding, 37

accumulation and neurodegeneration in the aging fly nervous system. 38

Results showed that phospho-mimicking Tau (hTau2N4RE14) induced profound 39

neurodegeneration, supporting a neurotoxic role for phosphorylation. However, deletion of the 40

aggregation-promoting 306VQIVYK311 motif in the microtubule-binding region altered the 41

conformation of Tau and neurotoxicity was completely abolished. Intriguingly, overt 42

aggregation of Tau into large filaments, detectable as HMW species in biochemical preps, was 43

not significantly reduced. Moreover, a peptide inhibitor targeting this same motif, that we have 44

previously shown to promote off-pathway Tau aggregation, efficaciously reduced Tau- 45

mediated behavioural deficits in aging Drosophila. 46

Collectively we show that neurodegeneration mediated by Tau hyper-phosphorylation 47

is gated via at least one aggregation-promoting motif of the protein, whether through a direct 48

impact on Tau aggregation or through suppression of other mechanisms of toxicity mediated 49

through this domain. Targeting the 306VQIVYK311 domain reduces the ability of hyper- 50

phosphorylated Tau species to acquire the pathological conformation responsible for inducing 51

neurotoxicity. This highlights the primacy of blocking the 306VQIVYK311 domain of Tau to 52

Introduction 56

The presence of highly phosphorylated, insoluble inclusions of the microtubule 57

associated protein Tau (MAPT) within neurons and/or glia of the central nervous system (CNS) 58

is a common pathological hallmark of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and other neurodegenerative 59

dementias collectively known as Tauopathies (1-3). Tau hyperphosphorylation and aggregation 60

are the two most prominent pathogenic hallmarks that influence Tau-mediated toxicity and 61

have therefore become the primary targets for modern Tau-based diagnostic biomarkers and 62

therapeutics (4, 5). However, the extent of their interdependence or relative contributions to 63

the progression of Tau-mediated toxicity, neuronal degeneration and disease progression 64

remains unclear. 65

Physiologically, Tau phosphorylation is implicated in the regulation of Tau- 66

microtubule binding (6), promoting microtubule assembly, stabilisation and spacing of the 67

microtubule network within neurons (7). However, a hallmark of the pathogenic process is Tau 68

becoming increasingly hyperphosphorylated (8), resulting in less  efficient binding to 69

microtubules and the induction of toxic consequences at the molecular, subcellular and cellular 70

level. In vitro studies have demonstrated that expressing phospho-mimicking Tau in neuronal 71

cells has a profound effect on neuronal structure and function, compromising cytoskeletal 72

integrity (9, 10), suppressing neuronal excitability (11) and inducing significant changes to the 73

normal subcellular localization and distribution of Tau (11-13). Similar deficits are reported in 74

vivo in Drosophila models of Tauopathy where driving hyperphosphorylation, by co- 75

expression of the Tau kinase GSK-3β, or emulating hyperphosphorylation by expressing the 76

phospho-mimicking TauE14 transgene disrupted axonal transport (14), reduced microtubule 77

binding (15) and induced significant neuronal and synaptic degeneration (9, 14, 16-19). In the 78

TauE14 transgene, key disease-associated serines and threonines have been substituted with 79

glutamate, with the charge on the latter mimicking phosphorylation. These manipulations 80

impair neuronal function in multiple ways and induce significant neuronal and synaptic 81

degeneration (9, 14, 16-19).   Moreover, expression of TauE14 resulted in greater accumulation 82

of Tau in sarkosyl insoluble cellular fractions and the formation of bona fide Tau aggregates 83

within fly brains (17, 20, 21). Furthermore, in FTD mouse models, transgenic Tau variants can 84

misfold and form pre-tangle-like fibrils, which can be significantly reduced with GSK-3β 85

inhibitor treatment (22-28). 86

Several species of aggregated Tau have been identified in both human brain and animal 87

Tauopathy models. However, the smaller hyperphosphorylated oligomeric aggregates are 88

thought to mediate toxicity (29, 30). The hypothesis that aggregation of these smaller Tau 89

oligomers mediates Tau toxicity is well-supported in cell culture models, presenting with 90

impaired synaptic function (13), cellular damage (31), disrupted cellular trafficking including 91

axonal transport (32), and induction of inflammatory responses (33). In addition, transgenic 92

animals over-expressing aggregation-prone Tau mutants and isoforms incur significant 93

neuronal degeneration paired with cognitive and locomotor deficits (15, 34-37). Such 94

aggregation-induced toxicity has been attributed to two hexapeptide motifs on the Tau protein, 95

denoted PHF6* (275VQIINK280) and PHF6 (306VQIVYK311) (37). When these hexapeptides are 96

deleted, or blocked by site-specific peptide-based drugs, cognitive deficits and reduced lifespan 97

are largely ameliorated in transgenic animals (38-40). 98

Several lines of evidence implicate Tau phosphorylation in promoting aggregation, but 99

the precise molecular mechanism underlying this interplay is not clear. Nonetheless, phospho- 100

epitopes of Tau influence its aggregation, either directly or by promoting phosphorylation at 101

additional sites (17, 41-46). The consensus view is that phosphorylation at residues that reduce 102

5

microtubule binding can encourage aggregation by enhancing the local cytosolic concentration 103

of free Tau, thus encouraging interaction with aggregation-promoting cofactors (47). 104

Alternatively, Tau phosphorylation may induce misfolding into seed-competent and 105

aggregation prone conformations (48, 49). Conversely, some studies show that 106

phosphorylation at certain sites appears to suppress further phosphorylation and aggregation 107

(45, 50-53). Complicating the picture further, there is some evidence to suggest that 108

phosphorylation may lie downstream of aggregation. Inhibition of aggregation through 109

306VQIVYK311 ablation and peptide-based drugs leads to reduced phosphorylation in in vitro 110

and in vivo models of Tauopathy (38, 39, 54, 55), suggesting that aggregation may in fact 111

promote phosphorylation. It is therefore unclear whether phosphorylation lies exclusively 112

upstream of aggregation or whether Tau can become phosphorylated to some extent after it is 113

aggregated. Such incongruency may arise from the use of different Tau isoforms in diverse 114

experimental systems which complicate comparisons between different studies addressing the 115

relationship between Tau phosphorylation and aggregation. 116

Beyond the potential causal and perhaps reciprocal relationship between Tau 117

aggregation and phosphorylation, interpreting the relative contribution of each pathological 118

modification towards Tau-mediated toxicity is challenging. This is because it is difficult, in a 119

single model, to independently and combinatorially manipulate phosphorylation, aggregation, 120

Tau expression levels and neuronal age, all of which contribute to degenerative phenotypes 121

(34, 56, 57). To resolve this conundrum, a systematic assessment of the aggregation- 122

phosphorylation interplay in a well-controlled in vivo experimental model is needed. 123

To address this problem, we assessed the relative contributions of phosphorylation and 124

aggregation on Tau-mediated degeneration using several novel transgenic Drosophila. A 125

number of novel human Tau (hTau) mutants were generated to determine toxicity of wild type 126

(WT) and phospho-mimicking Tau (hTau2N4RE14), and mutants with deletion of the 127

6

aggregation-promoting 306VQIVYK311 sequence in both WT Tau (hTau2N4RDEL) and 128

phospho-mimicking Tau (hTau2N4RE14/DEL) to enable the assessment of the toxicity of 129

phosphorylated Tau which cannot aggregate. We report that the expression of WT hTau2N4R 130

induced significant intracellular Tau accumulation and neuronal degeneration, which was 131

greatly exacerbated by the phospho-mimicking hTau2N4RE14 variant. However, deletion of the 132

306VQIVYK311 sequence completely abolished the toxicity of the phospho-mimicking Tau, 133

demonstrating that whilst hyperphosphorylation of Tau drives Tau-toxicity, this absolutely 134

requires the 306VQIVYK311 domain. Whether this domain mediates Tau toxicity exclusively by 135

directly promoting aggregation or additionally via indirect mechanisms involving interacting 136

proteins and induction of pathological conformations remains unresolved. 137

Results 139

Phosphorylation-dependent somato-dendritic and axonal degeneration requires the 140 306VQIVYK311 domain 141

To investigate the relative contributions of hyperphosphorylation and aggregation to 142

neuronal degeneration, we first generated a panel of 10xUAS-hTau2N4R transgenes with 143

specific mutation(s) and a single copy was integrated into the attP40 locus of the fly genome. 144

Thus, the mutants were expressed at similar levels in all experiments (Supplementary Fig. 1), 145

allowing quantitative comparison of their impacts. An additional advantage of this system is 146

that all transgenes are selectively expressed in well-defined neurons (Or47b olfactory sensory 147

neurons) offering segregation of neuronal compartments to facilitate assessment of Tau sub- 148

cellular localization and toxic effects in the soma, dendrites, axons and synaptic fields 149

(Supplementary Fig. 2). Or47b neuronal soma and dendrites are in the proximal region of the 150

antennae and their axons innervate and terminate in a specific antennal glomerulus bilaterally, 151

where they synapse with projection neurons relaying olfactory information to higher order 152

learning and memory centres (Supplementary Fig. 2). To identify neurons expressing the 153

7

Or47b-GAL4 driver, the membrane tagging UAS-CD8::EGFP transgene was recombined onto 154

the same chromosome. Thus, neurons expressing the novel Tau transgenes under this driver 155

were marked by GFP, while Tau expression and its effects were visualized by tracking the 156

cytoplasmic mCherry (i.e. mCherry::hTau2N4R). 157

We generated the following Tau mutant transgenic strains: UAS-hTau2N4R, the 158

phospho-mimicking mutant UAS-mCherry::hTau2N4RE14 in which phosphorylation at 14 159

disease-associated sites is physiochemically mimicked, the aggregation resistant mutant UAS- 160

mCherry::hTau2N4RΔVQIVYK in which the aggregation-promoting 306VQIVYK311 motif is 161

deleted (termed hTau2N4RDEL), and also a phospho-mimicking but aggregation resistant 162

mutant UAS-mCherry::hTau2N4RE14/ΔVQIVYK (termed hTau2N4RE14/DEL). 163

Consistent with previous studies, expression of hTau2N4R led to progressive and 164

quantifiable reduction in soma width that was significantly different from controls by day 14 165

(T14) (Fig. 1A6 versus Fig. 1A7, quantified in Fig. 1C). These somato-dendritic defects were 166

exacerbated in animals expressing the phospho-mimicking hTau2N4RE14 in which 167

neurodegeneration was significantly enhanced such that there was 23% soma loss by day 3 168

(T3) which increased to 36% by T14 (Figs. 1A4 and 1A9, quantified in Fig. 1B). Moreover, 169

the width of the soma in hTau2N4RE14-expressing neurons was also significantly reduced by 170

T3 and remained at this level at T14 compared to no Tau and hTau2N4R controls (Figs. 1A9, 171

quantified in Fig. 1C). 172

In the axonal compartment, Tau accumulation is reported to impair transport(14, 18) 173

resulting in axonal swellings leading to fragmentation and neuronal loss in mammalian 174

Tauopathy models(58-60). These morphological characteristics were also examined in hTau- 175

expressing Or47b neurons. Control Or47b neurons present with the typical compact highly 176

fasciculated axon bundles with some age-dependent swellings and defasciculation evident in 177

older animals (Fig. 2A1 and Supplementary Fig. 3A1). The number, size and total volume of 178

axonal swellings were greatly increased upon hTau2N4R expression at all ages assayed (Fig. 179

2A2 and Supplementary Fig. 3A2). As was seen in the somato-dendritic compartment, these 180

aberrant axonal phenotypes were greatly exacerbated by hTau2N4RE14 expression at all time 181

points. This was characterised by the appearance of prominent axonal swellings, fragmentation 182

and dystrophic processes in hTau2N4RE14-expressing neurons (arrow heads in Fig. 2A4 and 183

Supplementary Fig. 3A4), indicative of substantial axonal and synaptic loss. This is also 184

evident in a reduction of the total volume of the axonal bundle (Supplementary Fig. 4). 185

Both these data sets align with other studies indicating that Tau-mediated somato- 186

dendritic and axonal degeneration is driven by phosphorylation at sites known to be 187

phosphorylated in Tauopathies validating our novel experimental system. 188

As aggregation is also implicated in Tau-mediated degeneration and is believed to be 189

triggered by misfolding induced by Tau hyperphosphorylation, we next sought to investigate 190

the impact of reducing the aggregation propensity of hTau2N4R and of hTau2N4RE14. This was 191

achieved by deleting the 306VQIVYK311 domain in both Tau transgenics which are referred to 192

as hTau2N4RDEL and hTau2N4RE14/DEL respectively from here on. Both hTau2N4R-mediated 193

shrinkage of cell body width (Fig. 1A7 and 1C) and axonal swellings (Fig. 2A2) were 194

completely absent upon 306VQIVYK311 deletion both in hTau2N4RDEL (Fig. 1A8, Fig. 2A3, 195

Supplementary Fig. 3A3), and hTau2N4RE14/DEL-expressing animals at all ages tested (Fig. 196

2A5, Supplementary Fig. 3A5). The cell body widths and axonal profiles of both these 197

306VQIVYK311 deletion mutants were virtually indistinguishable from age-matched controls 198

(Fig. 2A1 and Supplementary Fig. 3A1). Quantification of axonal swellings and neuronal loss 199

further supports these conclusions (Fig. 2B and Supplementary Fig. 4). 200

Additional confirmation of these findings was afforded by Structured Illumination 201

Microscopy (SIM) which provides much greater subcellular resolution to visualise Tau- 202

mediated axonal degeneration. SIM imaging of the commissural tract located at the top of the 203

olfactory glomeruli at T14 clearly shows large axonal swellings and profound axonal loss in 204

the hTau2N4RE14 animals (Fig. 2A4’), which are completely attenuated upon 306VQIVYK311 205

deletion in hTau2N4RE14/DEL animals (Fig. 2A5’). 206

This shows that deletion of the 306VQIVYK311 motif renders the toxic hTau2N4R 207

protein benign, even in animals mimicking hyperphosphorylation at established disease- 208

associated sites. This implies that the toxicity of hyperphosphorylated hTau2N4R is mediated 209

by the 306VQIVYK311 aggregation promoting motif. 210

To test the specificity of this remarkable rescue of phospho-Tau-mediated toxicity by 211

deletion of the 306VQIVYK311 domain, the same Tau variants were expressed in developing 212

photoreceptors, using a GMR-GAL4 photoreceptor driver. Tau toxicity in photoreceptors 213

manifests as fusion, loss and disorganisation of ommatidia and sensory bristles (Supplementary 214

*Fig. 5), which can be assigned a ‘disorganization’ phenotypic score using Flynotyper(61). 215*

Expression of hTau2N4R led to a subtle eye disorganization (Fig. 2A7), which was 216

significantly exacerbated in the hTau2N4RE14 animals (Fig. 2A9). Reminiscent of the rescue 217

seen in the Or47b neurons, these eye phenotypes were also totally eliminated upon deletion of 218

the 306VQIVYK311 domain in both the hTau2N4RDEL and hTau2N4RE14/DEL animals (Fig. 2A8, 219

A10). Quantification of this data supports this conclusion (Fig. 2C). Collectively, these data 220

indicate that toxicity mediated by hyperphosphorylation of hTau is gated through the 221

aggregation-promoting 306VQIVYK311 domain in multiple neuronal populations. 222

Sub-cellular accumulation and mis-localisation of Tau requires the 306VQIVYK311 domain 224

Another hallmark of Tau pathology is its mis-localisation or mis-sorting from axonal 225

(62, 63) to the somato-dendritic compartments, where it accumulates in large insoluble 226

cytoplasmic hyperphosphorylated inclusions (13, 62-64). In the Or47b neurons, the hTau is 227

expressed throughout the soma, axons and dendrites (Fig. 3B, Fig. 4A, Supplementary Fig. 6). 228

However, in the somato-dendritic compartment, hTau2N4R appears to be more highly 229

concentrated within the dendrites that lie within the antennal sensilla (Fig. 3A1-A10), 230

indicating mis-localisation to this compartment. Within the dendrites hTau2N4R distribution 231

became uneven and fragmented from T3 to T14 (Fig. 3A2, A7, Supplementary Fig. 6A2, A7). 232

By comparison, dendritic mis-localisation was greatly exacerbated in an age-dependent manner 233

in hTau2N4RE14-expressing neurons (Fig. 3A4, A9, Supplementary Fig. 6A4, A9). However, 234

deletion of the 306VQIVYK311 domain either in hTau2N4R or hTau2N4RE14 led to a profound 235

reduction of this mis-localisation, as smaller and sparser Tau accumulates were observed within 236

dendrites (Fig. 3A3, A5, A8, A10). This is supported by quantification of the volume of hTau 237

in the dendritic compartment showing significantly greater dendritic accumulation in 238

hTau2N4RE14 compared to hTau2N4R, which was significantly reduced in hTau2N4RE14/DEL 239

(Fig. 3C). 240

In the axonal compartment, all hTau protein variants were uniformly distributed in 241

Or47b expressing axons and synapses at T3 (Supplementary Fig. 3B2-5).  However, by T14 242

relative to those accumulating hTau2N4R (Fig. 4B).  These pathological Tau accumulates were 246

Collectively then, the aggregation promoting 306VQIVYK311 domain drives somato-dendritic 253

mis-localisation and axonal accumulation of hyperphosphorylated Tau. 254

How does deletion of the 306VQIVYK311 motif prevent Tau-toxicity? 255

Our data thus far implies that the pathogenic mechanism employed by 256

hyperphosphorylation of Tau requires the aggregation-promoting 306VQIVYK311 domain to 257

mediate toxicity. The most parsimonious explanation for the rescue of Tau toxicity following 258

deletion of this domain is a suppression of Tau aggregation. To examine this, a sarkosyl 259

insolubility assay was used to fractionate monomeric, aqueous insoluble but sarkosyl soluble 260

oligomeric and sarkosyl insoluble fibrillar Tau species (65). At day 14, in all the animals, the 261

Tau expressed appears to exist mostly as monomeric and sarkosyl soluble oligomeric forms 262

with some Tau also appearing as fibrillar species (Supplementary Fig. 7A,B for representative 263

blot and 7C,D,E for quantification). To our surprise deletion of the 306VQIVYK311 domain in 264

hTau2N4RDEL did not alter the proportion of Tau in the sarkosyl soluble oligomeric or fibrillar 265

fractions compared to the hTau2N4R animals (Supplementary Fig. 7A,B). This is despite the 266

fact that there is significantly more neurodegeneration and accumulation of Tau in the Or47b 267

neurons in hTau2N4R animals when compared to the hTau2N4RDEL animals at this time point 268

(for example see Fig 1C and Fig 2B where the toxicity in hTau2N4R animals is significantly 269

greater than that in hTau2N4RDEL animals). In contrast, in the hTau2N4RE14 animals, there did 270

appear to be more fibrillar Tau when compared to hTau2N4R animals, which was reduced in 271

the hTau2N4RE14/DEL animals but this was not statistically significant (compare the bands in 272

hTau2N4RE14 versus hTau2N4RE14/DEL in Supplementary Fig. 7A,B). Overall, this collectively 273

implies that the 306VQIVYK311 domain may be enhancing Tau toxicity by promoting 274

aggregation only in the phospho-mimicking hTau2N4RE14 animals. It gates toxicity through 275

some other mechanism in the hTau2N4R animals. This is an important observation because 276

this domain has always been considered to be pathologically significant only because it is 277

through promotion of fibril formation, especially when Tau is hyperphosphorylated, this is not 279

To assess how else the 306VQIVYK311 domain gates Tau toxicity, we examined three 281

other potential pathogenic mechanisms: i) alteration of phosphorylation capacity, ii) alteration 282

of microtubule binding ability and iii) propensity to misfold and acquire pathogenic 283

conformations. 284

As Tau toxicity is clearly driven by its phosphorylation state, and some studies have 285

reported a direct relationship between aggregation and phosphorylation, such that the former 286

impacts the latter (38, 39, 54), we investigated the effect of deleting the aggregation promoting 287

306VQIVYK311 domain on subsequent downstream phosphorylation of Tau.  We used western 288

blot analysis to examine phosphorylated Tau (p-Tau) expression with classic antibodies AT8, 289

AT180, AT270, PHF-1, and Ser262, which detect p-Tau at AD-relevant epitopes 290

(Supplementary Fig. 8). Since TauE14 is mutated at most of these sites, antibody binding would 291

not occur, so we conducted the analysis in WT hTau2N4R and hTau2N4RDEL. After 14 days of 292

expression there was no significant difference in total Tau expression (Supplementary Fig. 8A) 293

which implies the 306VQIVYK311 domain did not alter the clearance of Tau. Moreover, the 294

phosphorylation of Tau at all epitopes tested; Ser202, Thr205, Thr231, Thr181, Ser396, Ser404 295

and Ser262 were unchanged by the 306VQIVYK311 deletion (Supplementary Fig. 8A, A’). This 296

implies that deletion of the aggregation-promoting 306VQIVYK311 domain does not change the 297

ability of Tau to be phosphorylated. Thus the reduced toxicity of hTau2N4RDEL compared to 298

hTau2N4R is not because of any change in phosphorylation status. 299

The 306VQIVYK311 domain is located in one of the four microtubule binding domains 300

of Tau, and though not directly thought to be in the microtubule-binding interface, it is believed 301

to play a role in regulating microtubule binding function (66). It is conceivable that deletion of 302

this domain renders the hTau2N4RDEL and hTau2N4RE14/DEL proteins functionally incompetent, 303

so their expression in the cells is inconsequential and does not cause any toxic gain or loss of 304

function effect. To test for this a simple microtubule binding assay was carried out and as shown 305

in Supplementary Fig. 9, the microtubule binding ability of all the Tau variants used in this 306

study are not different. These findings demonstrate that the 306VQIVYK311 deletion variants are 307

not biologically inert or nonfunctional proteins. Rather, they are expressed and retain 308

measurable cellular activity, indicating that the absence of toxicity cannot be attributed to a 309

trivial loss of function or failure to engage cellular pathways. 310

For over a decade there have many studies showing that soluble Tau oligomers, likely 311

which deletion of the 306VQIVYK311 domain conferred protection was through reduced 317

controls. After 14 days of aging, all the Tau expressing flies expressing exhibited some MC1- 321

colocalised strongly with mCherry::Tau and were primarily localised to the axonal terminals at 324

the periphery of the Or47b glomerulus, representing only a minor proportion of the total Tau 325

signal (Supplementary Figure 10. B2 versus B3, C2 versus C3, and E2 versus E3). MC1 326

Peptide inhibition of 306VQIVYK311 rescues Tau-mediated locomotor deficits 337

To explore the translational potential of targeting the 306VQIVYK311 domain, we tested 338

whether targeting it pharmacologically could suppress pathological manifestations of hTau. To 339

that end, flies expressing hTau2N4R pan-neuronally were fed a low-dose (0.08μM referred to 340

as LD) and high-dose (0.8μM referred to as HD) of an aggregation inhibitor peptide RI-AG03. 341

Designed especially against the 306VQIVYK311 domain, we have previously shown that RI- 342

AG03 effectively suppresses aggregation of hTau in vitro in a biosensor cellular model (40) . 343

This inhibitor is well tolerated and not toxic to Drosophila at the LD and HD doses we have 344

used in the present study (40). We studied the climbing ability of adult flies in a well-established 345

locomotor assay to assess the effects of hTau expression in aging flies (34, 38). We quantified 346

the height climbed by flies in a 10 second period and found that the climbing ability of control 347

flies declined progressively, by 30% over 35 days (Fig. 4C). In contrast, expression of 348

hTau2N4R reduced climbing efficiency by 40% at T1 and by 70% at T21 when compared to 349

age-matched controls (Fig. 4C).  By T35, hTau2N4R-expressing flies were unable to climb at 350

15

all. However, treatment with either the LD or HD of RI-AG03 significantly improved the 351

climbing ability of hTau2N4R-expressing flies, at every time point tested, though not to control 352

levels (Fig. 4C). There did not appear to be any greater improvement in the flies treated with 353

the HD compared to those treated with the LD of RI-AG03. Although the peptide targets and 354

inhibits the 306VQIVYK311 domain, its effects are unlikely to be as potent as the complete rescue 355

of toxicity we reported when this motif is deleted in hTau2N4RDEL-expressing flies (Fig. 1-4), 356

as drug efficacy is highly dependent on its stability, penetration, assimilation and 357

of the 306VQIVYK311 domain is an effective method to suppress aggregation-dependent Tau 359

phenotypes. 360

Discussion 362

Phosphorylation and aggregation are both established pathogenic post translational 363

modifications of Tau thought to play a central role in mediating Tau-toxicity. They therefore 364

represent significant disease-modifying therapeutic targets for the treatment of Tauopathies. 365

Yet the causal relationship between these distinct post-translational modifications and their 366

relative contribution towards Tau toxicity is not clear. Our study determines the relative 367

contribution of hyperphosphorylation and aggregation in Tau-mediated neurodegeneration in 368

aging Drosophila olfactory neurons. We show that 306VQIVYK311 is an excellent candidate for 369

therapeutic intervention in vivo, and provide novel data which shows that its targeting can 370

render even highly phosphorylated Tau species inert. Our data also indicates that this domain 371

is not necessarily gating toxicity simply by promoting aggregation of Tau into insoluble species 372

like fibrils. It is likely to also mediate toxicity through other, less understood mechanisms, that 373

begin with induction of a misfolded conformation. 374

Phosphorylation as a Key Driver of Tau-mediated Toxicity 376

We demonstrate that the pseudo-phosphorylated hTau2N4RE14 mutant significantly 377

exacerbates neurodegenerative phenotypes compared to hTau2N4R in various neuronal 378

compartments in a novel experimental system. This finding aligns with previous research using 379

TauE14 and other phospho-mimicking mutants which have consistently shown increased 380

neuronal loss and organizational defects when expressed in alternative Drosophila neuron 381

subtypes including the mushroom bodies (77), retinal neurons (20, 78), and circadian clock 382

neurons (79). However, focusing on Or47b neurons revealed not only severe morphological 383

deficits, such as profound loss of somatic and axonal tissue, but also subtler hallmark 384

manifestations more difficult to document in situ such as the marked increase in axonal 385

swelling size and frequency. 386

While TauE14 is an aggressive mutant mimicking extensive hyperphosphorylation akin 387

to that seen in AD, it effectively recapitulates the pathogenesis associated with pathological 388

Tau hyperphosphorylation. This underscores the causal role of the 14 GSK-3β phosphorylation 389

sites mutated in TauE14, in Tau-mediated toxicity and validates the focus on reducing 390

phosphorylation as a therapeutic strategy. Adding to this we now show, for the first time, that 391

the pathogenic potential of these sites requires the aggregation promoting 306VQIVYK311 392

domain. 393

The Critical Role of the 306VQIVYK311 Domain in Tau Toxicity 395

There is significant evidence suggesting that phosphorylation is a precursor for 396

aggregation. Using pseudo-phosphorylated Tau mutants, like TauE14, multiple groups have 397

identified a number of phosphorylation sites that act in concert to promote polymerization of 398

monomeric Tau (44-46, 51, 80-82). Other studies using TauE14 have shown increased levels 399

of Tau in sarkosyl-insoluble fraction in Drosophila suggestive of increased hTau aggregation 400

in these pseudo-mutants (20, 78). 401

Our data largely support these studies, and show that toxicity driven by 402

hyperphosphorylation is fundamentally dependent on the aggregation-promoting 403

306VQIVYK311 domain. Remarkably, deletion of this domain in both hTau2N4R and 404

hTau2N4RE14 almost completely eliminated toxicity, despite persistent presence of phospho- 405

mimicking epitopes at disease-associated sites. Consistent with our findings, a previous study 406

similarly showed that deleting the 306VQIVYK311 motif in a Drosophila model expressing 407

hTau0N4R attenuated Tau toxicity, rescuing retinal degeneration and shortened lifespan (38). 408

However, our data additionally suggests that the 306VQIVYK311 motif does not simply 409

promote aggregation of Tau; it likely mediates toxicity through additional, less studied 410

mechanisms, that begin with induction of misfolding and acquisition of a pathogenic MC1 411

positive conformation. Many physiological functions of Tau are highly dependent upon its 412

phosphorylation state and its conformation, including interactions with other cellular proteins 413

like RNA-binding proteins, molecular chaperones, signal and membrane-associated proteins 414

(83). Alterations to Tau’s global conformation mediated by mutagenic phospho-mimicking 415

mutations and/or deletions may very well shift the mutants interactome profile which may 416

directly or indirectly compromise binding of protective RNA-binding proteins and chaperones 417

such as G3BP2, Hsp27/70/90 and FKBP, which directly bind to the 306VQIVYK311 motif (84- 418

87). 419

Irrespective of the mechanism by which deletion of the 306VQIVYK311 motif protects 420

against Tau toxicity, our data highlights the therapeutic potential of targeting this domain in 421

vivo. Building on this, we provide novel insight into its critical role in the context of disease- 422

related hyperphosphorylation, suggesting that the gain-of-function (GOF) toxicity driven by 423

306VQIVYK311-dependent mechanisms surpasses any phosphorylation-mediated contributions 424

to overall Tau toxicity. 425

Implications for Therapeutic Strategies 427

Disease-modifying treatments for Tauopathies invariably aim to reduce pathogenic Tau 428

species, whether that is through anti-sense oligonucleotide (88) or vaccination (89) mediated 429

clearance, reduction of Tau phosphorylation through kinase inhibition (90-92) or suppression 430

of Tau aggregation using aggregation inhibitors (39, 40, 55, 93, 94). 431

Our findings have significant implications for the design of Tau-centred disease- 432

modifying therapeutics. While reducing phosphorylation remains a valid approach, our results 433

suggest that targeting the 306VQIVYK311 domain may be a more effective strategy to suppress 434

the toxicity of multiple pathogenic forms of Tau. This domain appears to be crucial for 435

pathogenic mechanisms downstream of hyperphosphorylation, beyond simply promoting 436

aggregation, in mediating the toxic effects of Tau. Indeed, several studies have reported 437

promising findings showing the neuroprotective effect of peptides targeting both the 438

306VQIVYK311 and the 275VQIINK280 domain. We also show that use of the peptide aggregation 439

inhibitor RI-AG03 (40) to pharmacologically recapitulate the deletion of the 306VQIVYK311 440

domain, reduces age-related Tau-mediated behavioural deficits. 441

Further studies should investigate other physiological and pathological functions of the 442

306VQIVYK311 domain including its interactome profile to understand how the deletion of this 443

motif confers protects. Additionally, exploring the effects of peptide aggregation inhibitors on 444

other neurobiological functions of Tau will be crucial for translating these findings into 445

effective therapeutic interventions. 446

Conclusion 447

In conclusion, our study provides compelling evidence that while Tau phosphorylation 448

is a key driver of toxicity, its pathogenic effects are primarily mediated through the 449

306VQIVYK311 domain. Though traditionally thought to promote aggregation, this domain may 450

mediate Tau toxicity through other, as yet well understood mechanisms as well. Importantly, 451

regardless of the level of Tau phosphorylation, targeting of this domain can effectively suppress 452

Tau toxicity in vivo. 453
